claim: Most users maintain home and office servers.
originalWording: Most users maintain home and office servers.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 8, printed p. 17

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Most users keep large personal digital collections on servers physically at home or in their offices.
reference.rationale: Home/network storage and office servers existed, but home servers were not the typical personal-computing model. Large digital collections and server-backed access are ordinary, but cloud hosting displaced much of the predicted home-server architecture.

evidence.title: Pew: Americans and their gadgets
evidence.note: US survey, seven broad device categories; median three categories. A proxy for device ownership, not a direct census of worn processors or 2009 body networks.. US survey, seven broad device categories; median three categories. A proxy for device ownership, not a direct census of worn processors or 2009 body networks.

evidence.title: Apple launches iPhone 4S, iOS 5 and iCloud
evidence.note: Announcement; retail availability October 14. This is NOT the first-ever voice assistant, nor the first standalone Siri release.. Announcement; retail availability October 14. This is NOT the first-ever voice assistant, nor the first standalone Siri release.

evidence.title: iTunes Store tops over five billion songs sold
evidence.note: Opening sales paragraph and descriptions of digital movie distribution. The release documents billions of digital song downloads and a substantial movie-download business. Evidence limits: This is digital-collection context only, not evidence of home-server ownership or the adoption denominator.

evidence.title: Microsoft unveils Windows Home Server at CES 2007
evidence.note: Simplifying Digital Life and Connecting Digital Devices and Experiences sections. Microsoft describes automatic PC backups, centralized home media and remote Internet access from a home-local server. Evidence limits: This adds direct architecture evidence. The January announcement projected release later in 2007 and supplies no evidence that most households adopted it.

evidence.title: Windows Home Server — Microsoft Lifecycle
evidence.note: Support Dates table: Windows Home Server start date. The official lifecycle entry gives 2007-10-11 as the product start date, corroborating a pre-2009 product timeline. Evidence limits: A support start date is not a retail shipment count or evidence of widespread home-server ownership.

broader.rationale: Cloud-backed libraries and synchronization realize the function. This deliberately relaxes the home/office location requirement.
